purpose: Source and decision record for the first instructional content drafts of the five September NOI courses.
scope: Draft descriptions, rationales, outcomes, objectives, topical and laboratory content, instructional methods, assignment examples, evaluation, and instructional resources. Include confirmed preparation decisions and AERO 100 content review for the three applications courses. These are not complete CurrIQunet submissions.
user_direction: Write concise, sensible, broadly framed content that preserves flexibility in teaching each course.
Use the user's notes and additional repository and Google Drive context. Take inspiration from AERO 100 and consult other independent study CORs.
Discuss missing substantive information before inserting it into the drafts.
AERO 161, AERO 162, and AERO 163 require AERO 100, with no additional AERO prerequisite.
AERO 151 laboratory work is mainly applied regulatory and safety exercises.
Assess students individually within shared crew projects in the three applications courses.
Leave the AERO 151 prerequisite open. Its draft deliberately omits a prerequisite entry rather than asserting that there is none.
drafting_choices: Use two assessable outcomes per course and a short objective set, following the compact structure of AERO 100.
Keep aircraft models, software brands, named field sites, fixed project specifications, and external certification requirements out of the instructional commitments.

Retain the September NOI scope. AERO 161 includes the orthomosaic workflow, GNSS, ground control, and independent accuracy checks. AERO 162 includes visible, multispectral, and thermal sensing and application placement. AERO 163 includes search, incident assessment, and photogrammetric scene documentation.

Use water for AERO 162 application exercises, consistent with the submitted October packet. The older agricultural pesticide licensing course is contextual material, not the specification for AERO 162.
Use the independent study agreement to define project-specific objectives, activities, reviews, resources, and evaluation. Do not make every independent study project a flight or mapping project.

The instructional resources paragraphs identify appropriate categories of materials. AERO 161 now specifies an instructor-developed primary resource. Published companion references remain recommendations pending selection. The other courses retain their initial materials placeholders.
remaining_administrative_work: Verify the post-September NOI workflow status and any subsequent curriculum changes before entering CORs.
Resolve AERO 151 preparation and any resulting formal requisite content review.
Confirm the independent study course number, formal preparation wording, and the applicable content review procedure for project-specific preparation.

Review AERO 147 enrollment and supervision with Ron and the curriculum office. The NOI proposes 25. The active ENGR 247 report has a cap and modality limits of 5. ATCH 147 shows modality limits of 1. These examples do not establish the required AERO limit.
Confirm the weekly hour entry convention under the 16-week calendar. Drafts preserve the NOI term hours and units.
Complete grading, modality and distance education fields, formal materials entries, resource and library responses, and other administrative fields before submission.
The September source still records blanks for dean or director approval date, qualified faculty response, and the independent study cap category.

aero_161_revision.user_direction: Use an instructor-made course materials document that can be digital or printed and is included in the class cost. Recommend a recent photogrammetry reference without making it a required purchase. Proceed with the handbook-based content revisions.
completed: Specify 2 lecture units and 1 lab unit while preserving the NOI term hours.
Describe reading, writing, and the 72 hours of outside work. Strengthen the two independent assignment examples.
Describe accessible materials, guided practice, equitable opportunities within crew roles, and appropriate ways to demonstrate reasoning.
Map each course objective to assessment evidence and criteria.
Specify the instructor-developed document as the primary resource, supplied in accessible digital and printable formats without a separate required textbook purchase.
remaining: The instructor-developed document is planned. It has not been authored or published. Record its actual title, author, version, date, and review access when available.
Kyle has not selected a published companion reference. The recommendations below are not adopted or required texts.

Complete local prerequisite validation and CurrIQunet field selections, including objective evaluation selections, grading, discipline assignment, outcome mapping, modality, library and resource responses, and the weekly hour convention. The Page remains an instructional content draft.

Confirm local acceptance of the representative materials package before submission. Seven years is Kyle's reference selection target. The older Cuesta form also asks for a rationale for textbooks over five years old.

reference_recommendations.author: Krystian Pyka
reference_recommendations.title: Basics of Photogrammetry
reference_recommendations.publisher: AGH University of Krakow, Open AGH
reference_recommendations.assessment: Best match for an accessible companion to the instructor document. The English textbook covers aerial image capture, flight planning, control, calibration, orientation, SfM, orthophotos, and measurement accuracy. The publisher lists 2026 for publication and update and offers PDF and EPUB formats. Metadata and chapter outline were checked. Full pedagogical and accessibility review remains to be done.

reference_recommendations.authors: Thomas Luhmann, Stuart Robson, Stephen Kyle, and Jan Boehm
reference_recommendations.title: Close-Range Photogrammetry and 3D Imaging
reference_recommendations.assessment: A substantial technical reference covering mathematical foundations, imaging, analytical methods, digital image analysis, and measurement quality. Better suited to instructor reference or selected advanced readings than the primary reading for this applied course. Close-range emphasis is less directly aligned with aerial orthomosaics.

reference_recommendations.author: Bon A. DeWitt
reference_recommendations.title: Elements of Photogrammetry With Applications in Drone Imagery
reference_recommendations.status: Forthcoming. Publisher lists March 5, 2027. Not available as of October 27, 2026 and not a current adoption recommendation.
